summary.text: Mike Cameron is a Republican state representative who has represented Georgia House District 1 since January 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Steven Disbrow.

paragraphs.text: Cameron was born in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and graduated from Lookout Valley High School in 1977.
He earned an A.S. in business from Chattanooga State University in 1979 and a B.A. in history in 1987, and his career experience includes working with Blue Cross Blue Shield of Tennessee.

Cameron won the 2020 Republican primary for House District 1, defeating Vikki Mills in the primary and John Deffenbaugh in the August 11 runoff, and then won the general election, taking office on January 11, 2021.
He defeated Jackie Harling in the 2022 Republican primary, won re-election that November, and defeated Jack Zibluk in the 2024 general election.
He defeated Neal Howell in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary.

For the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Agriculture and Consumer Affairs, Appropriations, Industry and Labor, Human Relations and Aging, Interstate Cooperation, and Rural Development committees, and he is vice chair of Human Relations and Aging.
